Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3 et seq. (offences of laundering proceeds); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 24; Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, ss. 20, 113, 114, 119, 121, 226, and records requirements; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21, 21.1, 23, 106, 140, 240; British Columbia Information Access and Protection of Privacy Act and Land Owner Transparency Act, S.B.C. 2019, c. 23 (for land holding filings).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each individual holding 25% or more of the target shares
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the individual's country of nationality; notarization performed by a licensed notary public or solicitor in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the document is issued or notarized in a Hague Convention contracting state; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Consulate of Canada or an authorized Consular Official of the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, bank statement, or equivalent government-issued correspondence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated bank, or government body in the UBO's country of residence; notarization by a licensed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable to the country of issue

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Corporate Registry Extract for any corporate legal entity UBO or intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry or corporate regulator of the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the jurisdiction of the registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Registered Officers/Shareholders List from the corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent, or legal counsel of the intermediate corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the certificate is issued in a Hague member jurisdiction; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Canadian diplomatic mission in the issuing jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (FINTRAC) politically exposed persons (PEP) framework, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian autonomous sanctions published pursuant to the Special Economic Measures Act, Canada's Criminal Code financing-terrorism schedule, and British Columbia's Beneficial Ownership Transparency regime. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, their family members, and close associates; adverse media and negative news searches are to be documented. No money transfer from an unresolved high-risk jurisdiction may be received before final clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia), accessible via the OneStop Business Registry platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names are accepted primarily in English or French; a French equivalent may be added to the articles. The legal element 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Limitée', or approved abbreviation must appear. Names in non-Latin scripts or foreign languages must first be translated into English or French and transliterated into Latin characters before NUANS search. A Name Search Report from NUANS is required for the intended corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant is issued a written refusal by the BC Registrar of Companies stating the statutory basis under the Business Corporations Act. Within 14 days of refusal, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request addressed to the Director, Corporate Registry, attaching a revised name or a legal memorandum overcoming the stated grounds. If the refusal is based on connotation or resemblance to an existing name, a new NUANS search should be used for the revised proposed name. The Director must issue a final administrative decision within 21 business days; thereafter, judicial review may be sought before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted in British Columbia as registered/records offices only when a physical street address in BC is maintained for service of process and the virtual office provider functions as the registered agent. Mail-forwarding-only virtual offices do not satisfy statutory commercial substance and will not be accepted for incorporation. The corporation must retain records at a location within BC and provide physical access on demand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% quantified risk of an unannounced on-site inspection by the British Columbia Registry, Canada Revenue Agency, or FINTRAC within the first 24 months for this SaaS analytics business; risk is elevated if the registered office is a shared virtual agent and the entity has foreign-derived revenues exceeding CAD 100,000 without substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (British Columbia), ss. 10-13 (incorporation), s. 22 (corporate name restrictions), and ss. 195-205 (statutory corporate records).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Articles filed electronically through the Corporate Online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. The BC Business Corporations Act permits incorporation with one or more shares without par value; no escrow account or capital deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Notice of Articles and Articles adopted by the incorporator are hereby ratified and accepted; RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 common shares without par value by the sole incorporator is approved, and share certificates shall be issued upon receipt of full consideration; RESOLVED, that the registered office at the address stated in the Notice of Articles is adopted, with the appointed registered office contact; RESOLVED, that Jane Doe (director) is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, John Roe is appointed Corporate Secretary, and the President is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting; RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open corporate bank accounts and execute SaaS vendor and customer agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Online portal, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online, complete the Name Reservation Request, list up to three proposed corporate names, and pay the applicable fee. The registry returns a Name Reservation Request number valid for 56 calendar days. Use this number in the subsequent incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Identification of incorporator (full name and residential address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on distinctiveness or confusingly similar grounds under s. 22 of the BC Business Corporations Act, submit a revised request with an alternative name; refusal does not prevent incorporation under a different name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel, with subsequent filing to BC Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles disclosing the registered office address in British Columbia, the authorized share structure (common shares without par value), and the proposed directors. Prepare the Articles setting out share rights, restrictions, and transfer provisions if any. Have the incorporator and each proposed director sign consents to act. No notarization is required for electronic filing; paper filings require witnessed signatures.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry pre-filing screening queries the documents, revise the Notice of Articles or Articles to conform to the BC Business Corporations Act and resubmit; no penalty attaches to pre-filing corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry, Corporate Online incorporation filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in with a BCeID account and initiate the incorporation filing, entering the Name Reservation Request number, uploading the executed Articles, and paying the CAD 350 statutory filing fee (approximately USD 256). The system issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a certified copy of the Notice of Articles upon completion; download and retain both instruments for the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each director
Payment authorization (credit card or online banking)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for deficient fields, correct the flagged items and resubmit within the validity period of the name reservation. If an error appears in an issued certificate, file a correction request with the Registrar under s. 246 of the BC Business Corporations Act together with the original certificate and a supporting affidavit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting at the registered office or by written consent. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering ratification of incorporation, issuance of common shares, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of officers. Issue share certificates to the subscriber and record the transfers in the share register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer cannot serve, pass a written replacement resolution and file a notice of change of directors with the BC Registry within 15 days; late filing is cured by filing the notice with the Registrar and paying the late-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the corporate minute book at the registered office in British Columbia containing the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, Articles, registers of directors and shareholders, and minutes of meetings. Maintain records in English and ensure availability for inspection as required by the BC Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate copy of Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a records inspection identifies deficiencies, prepare corrective resolutions approved by the directors, update all registers, and pay any administrative penalty assessed by the BC Registry; prompt voluntary correction normally precludes further sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and CRA Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through CRA Business Registration Online for a Business Number if one has not been issued automatically by CRA upon information exchange with the BC corporate registry. Register for a GST/HST account (required when taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000) and establish the corporate income tax account for T2 filings. Provide corporate identification and registered office details for verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA issues a review letter, respond within 30 days with certified corporate documents; late registration penalties under the Excise Tax Act can be mitigated through a voluntary disclosure application to the CRA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable — no provincial industrial licensing body exercises jurisdiction over ISIC 6201 software-as-a-service and analytics activities in British Columbia.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating or manufacturing permit required; if a physical office is leased, a standard Municipal Business Licence must be obtained from the host municipality (e.g., City of Vancouver) as an administrative formality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no Environmental Assessment Certificate or operational permit is triggered under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2002, c. 43, for a cloud-based software analytics business with no physical manufacturing or discharge activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to software operations; general office waste must comply with municipal waste collection bylaws and the BC Recycling Regulation (B.C. Reg. 449/2004) for electronic waste disposal; leased office HVAC and energy performance remain the landlord's compliance obligation under the BC Energy Step Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: occupancy permit and fire inspection clearance under the BC Fire Code for the registered office premises; structural load inspection is the landlord's obligation; occupational health and safety compliance under the Workers Compensation Act, RSBC 1996, c. 492, with WorkSafeBC, including ergonomic workstation assessments and a written workplace safety plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll and excise tax administration; principal portal is My Business Account via canada.ca/revenue-agency. British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation and Programs Branch, administers Provincial Sales Tax (PST) through eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in British Columbia, or incorporating a Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or British Columbia Business Corporations Act, obtains a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) through the one-stop business registration process. For a BC-incorporated corporation, the BN is generated automatically upon incorporation through BC Corporate Registry and is activated as the corporate income tax account (RC), GST/HST account (RT), and payroll account (RP) as required. Non-resident suppliers without Canadian incorporation may register directly with CRA using Form RC1 and receive a BN with a GST/HST program account. The BN serves as both the statutory tax identifier and the indirect tax VAT/GST identifier; there is no separate national tax card.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box regime exists. A Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer and cannot elect pass-through treatment under the Income Tax Act. For GST/HST purposes, closely related corporations that are registrants may jointly elect under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act to treat supplies made between them as being made for nil consideration, subject to conditions, and certain restructuring elections are available for transfers of business on a GST-neutral basis. These elections do not alter the entity-level income tax classification and Canada does not provide hybrid mismatch entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) and BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, mandatory registration is triggered once a person carrying on commercial activity in Canada makes CAD 30,000 or more of taxable supplies in Canada during the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in the current calendar quarter; this is the small-supplier threshold. For BC PST, no equivalent small-supplier turnover exemption applies; a vendor selling taxable goods, taxable software or taxable services at retail in British Columbia, or a non-resident vendor with B.C. sales of taxable digital products or software, must register as a PST vendor.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based tax clearance, or digital stamping for GST/HST or BC PST. Electronic invoices are permitted and acceptable to CRA providing they contain all prescribed information under sections 169 and 169.1 of the Excise Tax Act, including vendor name and BN, date of supply, description and GST/HST amount or rate. Voluntary electronic invoicing may use PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standards, but CRA approval or integration with a fiscal central clearinghouse is not required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST/HST applies to a supply of goods exported by the supplier where the goods are exported as soon as is reasonable after the supply and documentary evidence is retained. For an SEO content analytics and keyword analytics SaaS supplied to a non-resident, zero-rating applies to intangible personal property and services supplied to a non-resident who is not registered under the Excise Tax Act and who does not acquire the supply for use, consumption or enjoyment in Canada. The supplier must retain contemporaneous evidence establishing the non-resident status of the recipient, the place of supply, and the absence of Canadian use. Qualifying zero-rated exports entitle the registrant to claim input tax credits and obtain a net refund where GST/HST credits exceed GST/HST collected.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Customs Coding Form B13A), applicable to physical media or tangible components exported from Canada; for pure digital delivery, this item is not mandatory but IP-geolocation and download evidence must be preserved

Bill of Lading, electronic transport document, or carrier certificate of export for goods; for cloud SaaS, server and access logs demonstrating delivery of services or intangible property outside Canada
Commercial invoice and signed service contract identifying the non-resident customer, billing territory, and recipient's GST/HST registration status
Inward remittance certificate, bank transfer advice, or payment settlement records showing foreign collected proceeds attributable to the zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA will audit zero-rating claims and may deny the 0% rate where evidence fails to establish export or non-resident use; the result is reassessment of GST/HST at 5% plus interest under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act and possible civil penalties under sections 280 and 285. The normal reassessment period is four years, but misrepresentation, fraud, neglect or wilful default removes the limitation period, leaving the export zero-rating exposure open indefinitely. Deliberate false or misleading statements can lead to criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act, with fines and imprisonment, and corresponding PST penalties may be imposed by the BC Ministry of Finance under the Provincial Sales Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); monetary authority, with the Department of Finance Canada responsible for exchange rate policy and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulating federally incorporated banks; no standalone foreign exchange administration agency exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under IMF Article VIII. There are no statutory approvals for profit remittance, dividend distributions, or capital repatriation for Canadian corporations, subject to solvency tests under corporate law and applicable withholding taxes. Foreign exchange transactions are freely conducted by chartered banks and regulated financial institutions. Domestic and cross-border payments settle in CAD without quota restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export proceeds in Canada. Canadian-resident exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in non-resident or domestic foreign-currency bank accounts; conversion to CAD is voluntary. The cross-border movement of funds is monitored under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act for AML/ATF reporting, and customs declarations apply for physical currency, but no export surrender or exchange control requirement exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Fintech EMI entities incorporated outside Canada may provide ancillary cross-border payment facilitation, but they cannot accept CAD deposits or operate as deposit-taking institutions in Canada without being licensed as banks or credit unions. Non-resident EMIs providing money transfer, virtual currency dealing, or payment services to Canadian clients are required to register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and are subject to compliance oversight. Onerous MSB registration, Canada's restricted access to domestic clearing infrastructure, and correspondent banking hurdles materially reduce viability relative to tier-1 banks; they are best used as auxiliary collection or payout rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video-based KYC corroboration is generally accepted by major Canadian banks for low-risk corporate accounts, such as a BC-incorporated SaaS analytics company with identifiable ultimate beneficial owners. An in-person interview is not a legal mandate under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, but the bank may require in-person verification for non-resident directors, individuals with political exposure, or when the source-of-funds documentation is incomplete. To expedite onboarding, directors should be prepared for a video conference and provide stamped corporate documents and notarized identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners or directors residing in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of BC incorporation record from BC Corporate Online; register of individuals with significant control (ISC registry); valid passports and proof of residential address; corporate organizational chart evidencing 100% ownership; declaration of source of wealth and source of funds; letters of professional reference; no sanctions or adverse media explanations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital/software revenue model with cross-border online merchants and payment aggregators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business description, website and live platform access; sample end-user license agreement and SaaS subscription agreement; list of target geographies; AML/ATF risk assessment for the low-risk MarTech segment; FINTRAC MSB status confirmation if applicable; annualized revenue projections and transaction flow diagrams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume international wire activity or unexplained rapid fund movements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecast covering 12 months; invoices and contracts supporting trade payables or operational disbursements; documentation of relationship with counterparties (suppliers, platform partners); beneficial ownership declaration; board resolution authorizing cross-border payments; anti-money-laundering / sanctions compliance program with screening tools if the bank requires a higher control standard.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route for a parent/shareholder capital contribution is an inbound SWIFT MT103 wire designated as payment for 'share capital' or 'contributed surplus,' with a clear remittance reference and the BC company name. For CAD settlement into a domestic account, the bank routes via the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Real-Time Rail (RTR). No Bank of Canada approval is required for foreign direct investment or capital inflows under current Canadian exchange control rules; however, the Investment Canada Act may require post-activity notification if a non-Canadian acquires ownership of a Canadian entity above asset thresholds (generally higher for WTO investors, but commonly only a notification for SaaS development where no cultural/sensitive business is involved). The receiving bank performs FINTRAC reporting for electronic funds transfers and must verify the commercial purpose; accordingly the corporate treasury should prepare the shareholder resolution, subscription agreement, and bank source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements may be executed via SWIFT MT103 for supplier invoices and recurring software licensing payments; commercial letters of credit (documentary LCs) are used for high-value contractual deliveries requiring documentary control. Canadian banks provide foreign currency disbursement accounts in USD, EUR, GBP and mainstream Asian currencies. No export proceeds surrender timeline applies, and CAD is freely convertible at spot. All outbound payments are screened against OFAC and Canadian sanctions lists; payments to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions require internal governance approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market and non-convertible settlement currencies
Cross-currency swaps (including cross-currency interest rate swaps) for term funding and balance-sheet hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (for a BC-incorporated company; a federally incorporated CBCA entity files the BC Extraprovincial Annual Report instead)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: A BC company must file within 2 months after the annual anniversary of incorporation (e.g., July 31 anniversary means filing by September 30 each year). A federally incorporated extraprovincial company files within 2 months after the anniversary of its BC extraprovincial registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is recorded as not in good standing. Failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative strike-off and dissolution under the BC Business Corporations Act; restoration requires filing all delinquent annual reports, paying outstanding fees and restoration fees, and may result in asset escheat.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA Annual Return (applicable only if the entity is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the annual anniversary of the federal incorporation date; must confirm registered office, directors, and shareholders information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: There is no separate late filing fine; however, the Director of Corporations Canada may dissolve the corporation after two consecutive missed annual returns. Restoration requires an application, payment of outstanding fees, and compliance with applicable CBCA provisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and unanimous written shareholder resolutions (annual statutory corporate record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government agency filing; the minutes and resolutions must be retained in the statutory minute book at the BC records office and produced for inspection upon demand by shareholders, auditors, and regulatory authorities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: An AGM must be held at least once in each calendar year and no later than 15 months after the preceding AGM. A single-member company may satisfy this requirement by a unanimous written shareholder resolution dated no later than the required AGM date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to hold an AGM or obtain a timely unanimous written resolution commit an offence under the BC Business Corporations Act and may be personally liable to penalties; continued default supports regulatory strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC provincial corporate income tax filed in a single return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The T2 is due within 6 months after each fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end requires filing by June 30). The final balance-due day is 2 months after year-end, extended to 3 months for a qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per month, capped at 12 months; compounded daily arrears interest applies; repeated non-filing may trigger a punitive penalty and CRA legal collection enforcement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate income tax rate (15% federal Part I general rate plus 12% British Columbia provincial general rate); eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) benefit from an 11% combined rate on active business income up to CAD 500,000 (9% federal + 2% BC small business rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Relevant incentives include the federal SR&ED investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs; 15% non-refundable for large corporations) and the BC SR&ED tax credit (10% refundable for CCPCs on qualifying BC expenditures); accelerated capital cost allowance for computer software and data analytics infrastructure; 100% deductibility of Canadian intercompany service fees when arms' length; no patent box regime in Canada or BC. For a MarTech/SaaS analytics tool, the most material ongoing incentive is the SR&ED credit on qualifying algorithm and data-crawler development.
